Run one task of a bundle on the cluster

Source: R/hpc.R
run_hpc_task.Rd

Runs one task of a bundle written by write_hpc_bundle(): the fit of one model, or one refit of a model for cross-validation, without the units of one fold. It is called on a compute node of the cluster by the bundle's script task.sh, which Slurm runs once for each task of a job array, and is seldom called by hand.

Usage

run_hpc_task(
  dir = ".",
  stage = "fit",
  task = Sys.getenv("SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID")
)

Arguments

dir

A character string, the folder of the bundle. Defaults to the working folder, which is where task.sh runs it.

stage

A character string, "fit" (the default) for a fit, or "kfold" for a refit for cross-validation.

task

A single whole number, or a character string holding one, the number of the task among those of its stage, as the tables inputs/tasks-fit.csv and inputs/tasks-kfold.csv number them. Defaults to the number Slurm gives the array task, in the environment variable SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID.

Value

The path of the task's result, invisibly. A message says how the task ended. A task that fails is an error, raised after its reason has been written into results/.

Details

A fit is made as fit_hazard_models() makes it: with fit_hazard(), refused if it lost a chain, and cross-validated by importance sampling with loo_hazard(), leaving out the unit settled when the bundle was written. A refit starts from the model's fit, read from the result of its task, so it runs only once that fit has ended well, and it predicts the units left out as kfold_hazard() does. Each model is compiled once, by its fit, into a folder of its own under stan/ in the bundle, named after its fit task, where its refits find the compiled program; two models that share their Stan code, as two whose formulas differ only in the name of a covariate do, are therefore never compiled into one file at the same time. A refit draws the effects of the units it leaves out at random, with R's own generator; when the bundle was written with a seed, the refit sets R's seed from it and from the task's number, so that a refit run again gives the same estimate.

Before anything is fitted, the files of the bundle are checked against their checksums and the installed rTFT against the version that wrote the bundle; a task stopped by the second check is recorded as failed, with the reason. A task whose result is already in results/ is not run again, so the tasks of a stage can be submitted again to run only those that failed or did not finish.

Each task writes into results/: a record of when and where it started (fit-001.started, for the first fit), and when it ends, a record of how it ended (fit-001.csv) and, if it ended well, its result (fit-001.rds). The record of how an earlier attempt ended is moved aside when a task starts again (fit-001.previous.csv), so that a task running again is seen as started. A result is written under another name and renamed when complete, so a task stopped at the end of its wall time leaves no result that looks complete. Every result is stamped with the checksums of the bundle, so that collect_hpc() never assembles it with another bundle.

See also

write_hpc_bundle(), which writes the bundle, and hpc_status(), which says what each task has done.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# on the cluster, from the folder of the bundle; task.sh runs the same, with the
# number of the task given by Slurm
run_hpc_task(stage = "fit")

# the second fit of the bundle in the folder my-run, run by hand
run_hpc_task("my-run", stage = "fit", task = 2)
} # }
